maria (support): :rotating_light: Customer 87654 reporting timeouts and 429s when launching Dedicated jobs in na-central. They say jobs stall in PLACEMENT stage for >2m, then fail with "alloc failed: placement timeout". Can oncall take?
ajay (oncall): investigating, grabbing logs from placement service now. any recent capacity events in na-central?
leo (infra): saw a scale-up earlier but kube_node_autoscaler had backoff from noisy-tenant throttles. Posting pod/event snippet.
sarah (eng-sre): pinging autoscale logs. if autoscaler is backing off due to OOM/eviction loops from a tenant, we might be failing headroom checks. Can you paste the allocation error?
maria (support): customer copy: ``ERROR: allocation failed: 429 Too Many Requests - placement unable to find compatible GPU in pool 'dedicated-na-central-v2' after 120s``
ajay (oncall): quick check: placement-service returned 503 to api-gateway at 2023-11-02T14:02:13Z. Routing shows fallback attempts to na-west2 then failback.
opsbot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2023-11-02-NA-CENTRAL-PLACEMENT (sev3) — assigned to @ajay.
leo (infra): metrics: dedicated-na-central GPU free count dropped from 42 to 8 over 10m. One tenant (tenant-998) spawned many small low-priority jobs that pinned multiple GPUs and triggered eviction churn. I see high KV-cache spikes and hot PCIe.
sarah (eng-sre): that's the noisy-tenant signature. Autoscaler hit min_replicas guard because a lot of instances were marked unhealthy during eviction flapping. Batching controller also throttled new allocations to avoid OOM during node churn.
maria (support): customer says their SLA requires 95% placement success for reserved capacity. They have a Reserved Contract. We need a temporary reroute or manual backfill.
ajay (oncall): two immediate actions: 1) try manual split-placement to another reserve pool we control (na-west2 reserve) 2) attempt tenant-level throttling for tenant-998. Which do we prefer?
leo (infra): start with tenant throttling to free headroom in na-central. I can lower tenant-998 concurrency to 1 and mark their instances as low-priority for 10m. Doing it now.
leo (infra): ``kubectl annotate pod job-xyz tenant=tenant-998 priority=low --context=dedicated-na-central`` — applied. Expect freed GPUs in ~30-45s.
sarah (eng-sre): watch placement queue and free_gpu_count. Also check placement-service logs for the backoff vector: are we failing on capability matching or overall free count?
ajay (oncall): placement debug: ``placement_request{cpu:16,gpu:1,quantized:true,arch:ampere} -> candidates 3 -> matched 0 -> backoff: insufficient-headroom``
maria (support): update: customer tried one job after 40s and got placed. They still see increased latency for job startup (cold KV cache). They're asking for an RCA and temporary credit for degradation window.
sarah (eng-sre): root cause hypothesis: noisy tenant created eviction churn which tripped autoscaler and batching controls, causing temporary headroom undercount and placement backoff. Secondary factor: a recent scheduler change increased conservative headroom when host-metrics delayed by >10s.
ajay (oncall): reproducer notes: spun up 60 small jobs under tenant-998 with rapid retries -> observed placement backoff and autoscale backoff in logs. Steps:
for i in 1..60:
  curl -X POST /v1/dedicated/jobs -d '{"gpus":1,"image":"tiny","tenant":"tenant-998"}'
Result: placement failures, autoscaler logs show repeated scale-down/scale-up oscillation.
leo (infra): mitigation taken: throttled tenant, forced manual backfill from reserve pool, and applied temporary override to conservative_headroom=false for 5m to let placement be less strict.
deploy-bot: config change applied to placement-config: "conservative_headroom": false (rolled for 5m) by leo.
sarah (eng-sre): please keep that override limited. We'll run a controlled test to ensure we don't destabilize other pools. Next steps: 1) run telemetry to confirm freed capacity 2) audit tenant-998 workload patterns 3) recommend k8s QoS / job submission limits to prevent this class of issue
maria (support): communicated to customer: temporary fix applied, placement success restored; offering 1 day credit for impacted jobs. Customer accepted, wants formal RCA within 48h.
ajay (oncall): tagging for follow-ups: action_items: ["RCA writeup","rate-limit defaults for Dedicated reserved pools","improve autoscaler signals to ignore eviction-flapping tenants","customer credit processed"]
sarah (eng-sre): notes for RCA — include reproducible script, autoscaler backoff timeline, metrics: free_gpu_count, placement_attempts, pod_evictions, scheduler_headroom_value.
leo (infra): leaving this thread after stabilization. if placement backpressure returns, I'll trigger a full failover to na-west2 reserve and notify infra-team.
maria (support): thanks everyone. closing incident once RCA is posted. :thumbsup:
